who: Lawrence G. J. Duggan, historian of medieval and Reformation Europe at the University of Delaware, PhD Harvard.

evidence.says: The 2000–2001 personnel catalogue lists Lawrence G. J. Duggan as a history professor, PhD Harvard, specializing in the Renaissance, Reformation and medieval church.
The authority identifies Lawrence G. Duggan, author of Armsbearing and the Clergy, as professor of history at Delaware; it also gives the fuller name Lawrence Gerald James Duggan.

notes: Name, institution, doctorate institution and field agree; the contemporary catalogue places him at Delaware in Kucher's completion year.

who: Victoria Lorée Enders, historian of modern Spain at Northern Arizona University, PhD University of California, San Diego.

evidence.says: The authority links Victoria Lorée Enders to Jaime Vicens Vives (1984) and Constructing Spanish Womanhood (1998); the latter identifies her as associate professor of history at Northern Arizona University.
The university catalogue lists Victoria Enders on the history faculty, with a UC San Diego PhD dated 1985 and specialties in Spanish and European intellectual history.
The publisher-supplied 1998 author biography identifies Victoria Loree Enders as associate professor of history at Northern Arizona University.

notes: Full name, department and doctorate institution agree. The NAU catalogue dates the PhD 1985, whereas AHA gives 1984; LC also records the dissertation work in 1984.

who: Sandra I. Enríquez, historian of modern US and public history at the University of Missouri–Kansas City, PhD Houston 2016.

The authority cites The Urban West at the End of the Frontier (2020), identifying Sandra I. Enríquez as assistant professor of history and director of public history at UMKC.

notes: The authority places the candidate in the same department immediately before Williams's 2021 completion; the doctorate matches exactly.

who: Tanisha C. Ford, historian of social movements, material culture and girlhood, formerly at Delaware, PhD Indiana 2011.

evidence.says: The authority cites Soul Generation (2011) as Tanisha C. Ford's Indiana University history PhD and a 2019 Delaware faculty page naming her associate professor of Africana studies and history.

The 2018–2019 fellowship biography places Tanisha C. Ford at Delaware in Africana studies and history, confirms her Indiana history PhD, and lists girlhood and material culture among her research interests.

notes: The full-name candidate matches the doctorate and Delaware faculty career. Her Delaware appointment is documented before Barnes's 2023 completion.

who: David Fors Freeman, historian of early modern Europe and the Dutch Atlantic at UMKC, PhD history, Emory 2002.

evidence.says: UMKC identifies David Freeman as associate professor of history and religious studies, teaching early modern Europe and Christianity, with an Emory history PhD dated 2002.
The university's 2012–2013 personnel report lists David Fors Freeman as assistant professor in History at the Kansas City campus.
The authority identifies David Fors Freeman from the title page of Wesel and the Dutch Revolt (2002).
The bibliography identifies David Fors Freeman's Wesel and the Dutch Revolt: The Influence of Religious Refugees on a German City, 1544–1612 as an Emory PhD dissertation, 2002.
The candidate receiving the automatic employer agreement is a painter and Winthrop art professor, with master's degrees from Iowa and Missouri.

notes: Select the David Fors Freeman candidate. The automatically favored painter is a different person. UMKC and the dissertation bibliography give 2002 for the Emory doctorate, versus AHA's 2003.

who: Mary T. (Mary Tibbetts) Freeman, historian of slavery and abolition at the University of Maine, PhD Columbia 2018.

evidence.says: The authority identifies Mary T. Freeman and Mary Tibbetts Freeman as the same author of Abolitionists and the Politics of Correspondence, an assistant professor of history at Maine.
A 2020 event biography identifies Mary Freeman as assistant professor of history at Maine, a Columbia PhD, researching slavery, abolition and antislavery letter writing.
Columbia University Libraries identifies Mary Freeman as having earned her history PhD at Columbia in 2018.

notes: The full-name authority matches Maine affiliation, research topic and the Columbia doctorate; she was at Maine before O'Hara's 2024 completion.

who: Joshua Frens-String, historian of modern Latin America and Chile at UT Austin, PhD NYU 2015.

His university-hosted CV lists a 2015 NYU PhD in Latin American history and appointments at UT Austin as assistant professor in 2017–2024 and associate professor from 2024.

notes: Name, institution, field and doctorate agree; his UT Austin appointment covers Stone's 2023 completion.

who: Kim T. Gallon, historian of the Black press and digital humanities, formerly at Purdue, PhD Pennsylvania 2009.

evidence.says: The authority connects Kim T. Gallon's Between Respectability and Modernity (2009) with Kim Gallon's Pleasure in the News (2020), identifying the latter's author as a Purdue history professor.
Purdue's 2020 promotion profile identifies Kim Gallon as a history faculty member with a Pennsylvania history PhD, researching the early twentieth-century Black press.
Purdue's 2014 new-faculty announcement identifies Kim Gallon as assistant professor in African American women's history, with a Pennsylvania doctorate dated 2009.

notes: The authority's initialed name and works match the Purdue historian; department and doctorate agree. Purdue employment is documented before Amoh's 2023 completion.
